newsitem.title: CHINA: China's huge Ertan dam on schedule, newspaper says.
newsitem.headline: China's huge Ertan dam on schedule, newspaper says.

text.p: China's second-biggest hydropower project, the giant Ertan dam in southwestern Sichuan province, is on schedule to begin producing electricity in October 1998, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The 240-metre-tall dam across Sichuan's Yalong River would have generating capacity of 3,300 megawatts and would produce 17 billion kilowatt hours of electricity a year, said the newspaper, which is published by the official China Daily.
The dam would be China's second-biggest, after the Three Gorges project on the Yangtze River, it said.
The Ertan dam's first turbine was expected to begin operating in July 1998, with electricity generation to begin in October the same year, it said.
All six of the dam's generators were expected to be onstream by the first half of 2000, it said.

The Ertan Hydropower Development Co Ltd, which is responsible for building and operating the project, had begun preparatory work to build four more dams along the Yalong with total capacity of 7,500 megawatts, it said but gave no details.
